candidates.title: Slovenia approves FSD Supervised as 6th EU member — 28 days before Oct 6 bloc-wide vote
candidates.whyItMightMatter: Sixth national approval ahead of the October 6 TCMV vote; six approved countries still cover only ~9% of the 65% population threshold needed to pass

candidates.title: Tesla FSD clears six EU nations but speed-offset fight could kill October 6 vote
candidates.whyItMightMatter: Details October 6 TCMV vote mechanics (15 states + 65% population required) and identifies speed-offset setting as the political blocker; Germany, France, Italy, Spain uncommitted

candidates.title: Tesla releases EU FSD safety evidence ahead of Oct 6 vote — all data closes before April 2026
candidates.whyItMightMatter: First public disclosure of the safety file underpinning Dutch RDW approval; data predates the European rollout it is meant to justify, which may weaken the October vote

candidates.title: Tesla issues ~5,000-unit Optimus component batch order to T-chain suppliers
candidates.whyItMightMatter: First production-scale procurement order (vs. prior hundreds-unit pilot runs); targets 1,000 units/week by late September, 2,500/week by year-end — still unconfirmed by Tesla

candidates.title: FSD v14.3.9 with Automatic Collision Evasion rolls out broadly to owners via 2026.27.6
candidates.whyItMightMatter: Broadens ACE from employee fleet to customer vehicles on HW4; adds highway evasive-steering and re-engagement when driver inattention detected — distinct from last week's employee-only preview

candidates.title: Ashok Elluswamy previews FSD v15: 'even earlier hazard prediction, significantly better collision avoidance'
candidates.whyItMightMatter: First on-record Ashok statement positioning v15 as a safety step-change, not just capability; company already running early v15 on Robotaxi fleet while customer cars are still on v14.3.9

candidates.title: HW3 Model S and X to receive FSD v14 Lite 'soon' — Ashok told Ryan McCaffrey at Cybercab launch
candidates.whyItMightMatter: Closes the last major HW3 gap in the v14 Lite rollout; S/X discontinued in May 2026 yet still awaiting the update that reached most other HW3 cars months ago

candidates.title: Samsung Taylor fab reaches full capacity before trial ops — AI5 2nm yield hits 80%, mass production 2027
candidates.whyItMightMatter: Taylor fab booked solid on Tesla AI5/AI6, Broadcom, and Arm orders before first wafer; 2nm yield up from 60% to 80%; trial ops begin 'early next month' with volume production 2027

candidates.title: Cybertruck + Powerwall 3 integration goes live — extends home backup 3+ days, three years after promise
candidates.whyItMightMatter: First vehicle-plus-home-battery bidirectional integration of this scale; originally promised at Cybertruck launch Nov 2023; Powerwall 2 and Powerwall+ compatibility still pending later this year

candidates.title: Goldman Sachs holds Tesla Neutral at $360 as Musk claims Cybercab 5x faster to produce than conventional cars
candidates.whyItMightMatter: Goldman's analysis pins Cybercab's $0.05–$0.30/mile cost edge on lower vehicle cost, but flags software scalability as the swing factor; Musk's 5x production claim lacks a unit or context

candidates.title: Tesla Cybercab Japan tour opens in Tokyo — display only, no rides, no approval
candidates.whyItMightMatter: First public Cybercab appearance in Japan across four cities (Tokyo, Osaka, Nagoya); frames potential market interest but no regulatory pathway or launch timeline announced
